summary: Standards (scenario atip.inputorder.10, brief F6): the test sets CANON_ACTOR=bob, a value the option accepts, so it proves the document's key wins over the variable but not that the variable is never validated when the document gives the key (what L2.input-env judges: a variable the option refuses). canon has no integer option that reads an environment variable, so the brief's literal case (an integer variable) cannot be made; the refusable case that exists is CANON_ACTOR on a relayed approval (one word). I ran it on the real binary: brief approve --input with a document actor and CANON_ACTOR='two words' answers as without the variable (CONFIG_MISSING after the stateless stage), and without the actor key it is USAGE /actor 'must be one word', so the behaviour holds; the test does not pin it. Blast radius: a change that validated the variable before the merge would pass 10.
